name: Isaac Morley
role: Kirtland farmer, bishop’s counselor, and later patriarch
dateNote: He was baptized on 15 November 1830, and the Morley farm was ordered sold in September 1831.
importance: Early converts and the New York Saints gathered on his Kirtland farm. Section 52 sends him with Ezra Booth to Missouri in June 1831. Section 64 says he and Booth had kept neither law nor commandment, but that Morley was forgiven. It explains that his farm was sold so he would not be tempted beyond what he could bear.
connections: He was a counselor to Bishop Edward Partridge in Ohio and Missouri. Titus Billings married his younger sister Diantha and cared for the farm.
reviewNote: Birth, death (24 June 1865, Fairview, Utah), baptism, counselor role, and later life checked on JSP. Sister relationship with Diantha Morley Billings from Wikipedia. Section 63 names only Titus Billings, not Morley.
